root_cause: Freshness was previously coupled to restorable data-path state rather than a signing-authority boundary.
Multi-file persistence had no durable protocol for crashes after literature persistence or between state and authentication replacement.
Long-lived runners could authenticate against a stale in-memory LiteratureBase snapshot.
EXISTING_OBSERVED validation required the input observation ID to equal the persisted record ID even when the logical and content bindings matched.
Topic state validation used weaker pathname checks than the authentication/signing boundary and was exposed to symlink and mode-policy gaps.
Source identity lowercased case-sensitive URI paths and used delimiter concatenation, allowing identity collisions.
design: Source logical identity and idempotency keys use canonical structured JSON; URI scheme and host are normalized while path case is preserved, and embedded delimiters remain unambiguous.
Topic persistence uses a private, explicitly versioned transaction journal with PREPARED and COMMIT_INTENT phases. It records complete old and target state, authentication, and literature snapshots.

A freshly generated private signing key is atomically replaced last and acts as the commit authority. Recovery accepts only a complete rollback or complete target generation whose key digest matches the journal; same-user access to the signing authority remains outside the threat boundary.
Restart preparation and public next_cursor/manual_queue reads reload LiteratureBase while holding the runner lock, and authenticated state validation rejects mixed or stale tuples.
EXISTING_OBSERVED permits a different persisted observation ID only when logical identity, content digest, artifact, and idempotency bindings match, preserving deterministic replay across restart.

State, authentication, signing-key, journal, and literature file reads enforce descriptor-based regular-file and private-mode checks, with O_NOFOLLOW where available; incompatible state remains fail-closed.
